eyebrow: What happens after the Born rule

steps.label: The Born rule gives probabilities — not the post-measurement state
steps.sub: Collapse is a separate, additional postulate

steps.label: Measuring the same qubit again gives 0 again
steps.sub: With probability 1 — the randomness was a one-time event

steps.label: Before measuring, a and b encoded a rich description
steps.sub: Magnitude and relative phase — continuous, information-rich

steps.label: After collapse, all of that is gone
steps.sub: You cannot work backward from |0⟩ to recover a and b

steps.label: No gate, no trick, no post-processing undoes it
steps.sub: That specific superposition's information is gone for good

steps.label: Measuring mid-circuit "just to check" destroys the work
steps.sub: It collapses whatever superposition the earlier gates built

steps.label: Algorithms build the full superposition uninterrupted
steps.sub: And measure only once, at the very end

steps.label: This previews chapter 5's no-cloning theorem
steps.sub: If you could copy a qubit first, you could dodge collapse entirely — nature forbids that too

subtitle: Measuring in a different basis is a real design decision, not a notational trick.
